scenarios.title: A permanent that is already tapped cannot be tapped to pay a cost
decisions: A considers activating Prodigal Sorcerer's ability ({T}: 1 damage to any target) targeting Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: untapped
variants.expected: The activation is legal: can_play is true, the cost {T} is payable, and Grizzly Bears is a legal target.

variants.label: tapped
variants.delta: Prodigal Sorcerer starts tapped.
variants.expected: The activation is not legal: can_play is false because {T} cannot be paid by a permanent that is already tapped.

scenarios.title: Paying life subtracts it from the life total, and a player cannot pay more life than they have
decisions: A activates Greed ({B}, Pay 2 life: draw a card), tapping Swamp for {B} and paying 2 life.
Both players pass; the ability resolves.

variants.label: five_life
variants.expected: A pays 2 life, going from 5 to 3. The ability resolves and A draws an Island; A's hand holds 1 Island and the library 1.

variants.label: two_life
variants.delta: A's life total is 2.
variants.expected: A pays 2 life, going from 2 to 0. In the state-based check before A next receives priority, with the ability still on the stack, A loses the game; the Island is never drawn.

variants.label: one_life
variants.delta: A's life total is 1.
variants.expected: The activation is not legal: A cannot pay 2 life with a life total of 1. Swamp stays untapped, A's life stays 1 and nothing is drawn.

scenarios.forge_notes: Library lists the top card first.

scenarios.title: Mana left in the pool after a payment stays available for the next payment
decisions: A taps both Mountains for mana, so A's pool holds {R}{R}.
A casts Shock targeting player B, paying {R} from the pool; {R} remains in the pool.
A casts a second Shock targeting player B, paying the remaining {R} from the pool.
Both players pass; the second Shock resolves, then the first resolves.

variants.label: excess_floats
variants.expected: Paying the first Shock removes exactly {R} from the pool, leaving {R}. The second Shock is castable with that mana. Each Shock deals 2 to B, so B is at 16.

variants.label: no_excess
variants.delta: One Mountain starts tapped, so only one Mountain is tapped for mana and the pool holds {R}.
variants.expected: Paying the first Shock removes the only {R} from the pool, leaving it empty. The second Shock cannot be cast (can_play is false). Only the first Shock resolves, so B is at 18.

scenarios.forge_notes: Both Mountains are listed untapped in the base setup; the no_excess variant starts the second one tapped.

scenarios.title: A spell with no mana cost has an unpayable cost and cannot be cast from hand
decisions: A considers casting Ancestral Vision from hand with four untapped Islands.

variants.label: no_mana_cost
variants.expected: Ancestral Vision cannot be cast: can_play is false, because its cost is unpayable. The four Islands stay untapped.

variants.label: with_mana_cost
variants.delta: A's hand holds Divination ({2}{U}) instead of Ancestral Vision.
variants.expected: Divination is castable: can_play is true, with a cost of {2}{U}.

scenarios.forge_notes: Suspending Ancestral Vision is a special action, not casting, so it is not the thing under test.

scenarios.title: An unpayable cost stays unpayable when increased, but a cast-for-free permission makes it payable
decisions: A considers casting Ancestral Vision from hand, using Omniscience's permission to cast it without paying its mana cost and paying Sphere of Resistance's {1} increase with Island.

variants.label: omniscience_pays_tax
variants.expected: Ancestral Vision is castable: can_play is true, with a cost after adjustment of {1} (only the Sphere increase), paid by tapping Island.

variants.label: no_omniscience
variants.delta: Omniscience is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Ancestral Vision cannot be cast: can_play is false. The cost is unpayable and stays unpayable under Sphere of Resistance's increase, even with an untapped Island.

variants.label: no_mana_for_increase
variants.delta: Island starts tapped.
variants.expected: Ancestral Vision cannot be cast: can_play is false. The free-cast permission applies, but the {1} increase from Sphere of Resistance cannot be paid.

scenarios.forge_notes: Depends on Forge applying Sphere of Resistance's RaiseCost to a MayPlayWithoutManaCost cast.

scenarios.title: A cost reduction lowers the amount actually paid
decisions: A casts Hill Giant ({3}{R}) paying its reduced cost with three Mountains.

variants.label: with_medallion
variants.expected: Ruby Medallion reduces Hill Giant's cost to {2}{R}. The cast is legal and all three Mountains are tapped. Hill Giant resolves and enters the battlefield.

variants.label: two_lands
variants.delta: Only two Mountains are on the battlefield.
variants.expected: The reduced cost {2}{R} needs three mana and A has two, so Hill Giant cannot be cast (can_play is false).

variants.label: no_medallion
variants.delta: Ruby Medallion is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Hill Giant costs {3}{R}, which three Mountains cannot pay, so it cannot be cast (can_play is false).

scenarios.title: A generic cost reduction cannot reduce the colored part of a cost
decisions: A considers casting the red creature in hand with Ruby Medallion and one untapped Mountain.

variants.label: all_colored
variants.expected: Ruby Medallion's {1} reduction cannot touch colored mana and Ember Hauler's cost {R}{R} has no generic part, so the cost stays {R}{R}. One Mountain cannot pay it: can_play is false.

variants.label: generic_present
variants.delta: A's hand holds Goblin Piker ({1}{R}) instead of Ember Hauler.
variants.expected: The {1} reduction removes the generic part, so Goblin Piker costs {R}. The cast is legal (can_play is true), the Mountain is tapped and Goblin Piker resolves onto the battlefield.

scenarios.title: A reduction by colored mana the cost does not require reduces generic mana instead
decisions: A casts Mirror Entity ({2}{W}), a Goblin spell through changeling, paying its reduced cost with the two Plains.

variants.label: no_red_in_cost
variants.expected: Goblin Influx Array reduces by {R}, but Mirror Entity's cost has no {R}, so the generic part drops by one. The cost is {1}{W}, both Plains are tapped, and Mirror Entity resolves.

variants.label: no_array
variants.delta: Goblin Influx Array is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Mirror Entity costs {2}{W}, which two Plains cannot pay, so it cannot be cast (can_play is false).

variants.label: red_in_cost
variants.delta: A's hand holds Goblin Piker ({1}{R}) instead of Mirror Entity.
variants.expected: The {R} reduction removes the {R} component. Goblin Piker costs {1}, paid by tapping one Plains, and it resolves.

scenarios.title: A single colored reduction that exceeds the cost's colored component also reduces generic mana

setup.notes: Both Islands are tapped and carry one flood counter each; A has no untapped land. A has cast no spell this turn.

decisions: A casts Impulse ({1}{U}), its first instant or sorcery spell this turn, paying the reduced cost with no mana.
Both players pass; Impulse resolves and A puts the top Island into hand, the other three on the bottom.

variants.label: two_flood_lands
variants.expected: Eluge reduces the cost by {U}{U}, which exceeds Impulse's single {U}: the {U} is removed and the excess {U} reduces the generic part by 1. The cost is {0}, can_play is true, and Impulse resolves; A's hand holds one Island.

variants.label: one_flood_land
variants.delta: Only one of the two Islands has a flood counter.
variants.expected: The reduction is {U}, which removes the {U} without exceeding it. The cost is {1} and A has no untapped land, so Impulse cannot be cast (can_play is false).

scenarios.forge_notes: Eluge's ReduceCost carries Amount$ Y (lands with a flood counter) and Color$ U, so one static reduces by {U}{U}. The flood counters are set up directly; whether the Islands are Islands through Eluge's effect does not matter here.

scenarios.title: An additional cost paid for a spell leaves its mana value unchanged
decisions: A casts Burst Lightning ({R}) with kicker {4}, paying 5 mana by tapping all five Mountains, targeting player B.
B responds by casting Mental Misstep on Burst Lightning, paying {U} by tapping Island.
Both players pass and the stack resolves.

variants.label: mental_misstep
variants.expected: Mental Misstep targets Burst Lightning legally, because the kicker did not change its mana value of 1. Burst Lightning is countered and goes to A's graveyard. B stays at 20.

variants.label: spell_snare
variants.delta: B's counterspell is Spell Snare (counter target spell with mana value 2) instead of Mental Misstep.
variants.expected: Spell Snare cannot legally target Burst Lightning, whose mana value is 1 although A paid 5 mana. Burst Lightning resolves kicked and deals 4 damage to B, leaving B at 16.

scenarios.title: Only one alternative cost can be applied to a spell as it is cast
decisions: A casts Fireblast ({4}{R}{R}) targeting player B, applying only Omniscience's permission to cast it without paying its mana cost.
Both players pass; Fireblast resolves.

variants.label: omniscience_only
variants.expected: Fireblast is cast for no cost. Both Mountains stay on the battlefield. Fireblast deals 4 damage to B, leaving B at 16.

variants.label: sacrifice_only
variants.delta: A applies only Fireblast's own alternative cost, sacrificing two Mountains, instead of Omniscience's permission.
variants.expected: Both Mountains are sacrificed and go to A's graveyard. Fireblast deals 4 damage to B, leaving B at 16.

variants.label: both
variants.delta: A proposes both alternative costs at once, sacrificing two Mountains and casting without paying the mana cost.
variants.expected: The attempt is not legal as proposed: only one alternative cost can apply, so the two cannot be combined. Fireblast can be cast with either one alone.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge offers each alternative as a separate way to play Fireblast, so the both variant may not be reachable; it is the playability verdict on the combination.

scenarios.title: An alternative cost leaves the spell's mana value unchanged
decisions: A casts Ancient Grudge ({1}{R}) from the graveyard for its flashback cost {G}, tapping Forest, targeting Ruby Medallion.
B responds by casting Spell Snare on Ancient Grudge, tapping Island for {U}.
Both players pass and the stack resolves.

variants.label: spell_snare
variants.expected: Spell Snare targets Ancient Grudge legally: its mana value is 2 even though A paid only {G}. Ancient Grudge is countered and exiled (flashback). Ruby Medallion stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: mental_misstep
variants.delta: B's counterspell is Mental Misstep (counter target spell with mana value 1) instead of Spell Snare.
variants.expected: Mental Misstep cannot legally target Ancient Grudge, whose mana value is still 2. Ancient Grudge resolves and destroys Ruby Medallion, which goes to B's graveyard; Ancient Grudge is exiled (flashback).

scenarios.title: Cost increases apply on top of an alternative cost
decisions: A casts Fireblast targeting player B, paying its alternative cost (sacrificing two Mountains) and any cost increase with Island.
Both players pass; Fireblast resolves.

variants.label: increase_paid
variants.expected: Sphere of Resistance adds {1} to the alternative cost. A sacrifices both Mountains and taps Island for {1}. Fireblast resolves and deals 4 damage to B, leaving B at 16.

variants.label: island_tapped
variants.delta: Island starts tapped.
variants.expected: The {1} increase cannot be paid on top of the alternative cost, so Fireblast cannot be cast (can_play is false). Both Mountains stay on the battlefield and B stays at 20.

variants.label: no_sphere
variants.delta: Sphere of Resistance is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: No increase applies. A sacrifices both Mountains, pays no mana (Island stays untapped), and Fireblast resolves, leaving B at 16.

scenarios.title: One sacrifice cannot pay the costs of two abilities
decisions: A activates Viscera Seer's ability (sacrifice a creature: scry 1), sacrificing Viscera Seer itself.
With that ability on the stack, A considers activating Goblin Bombardment (sacrifice a creature: 1 damage to any target) targeting player B.

variants.label: only_one_creature
variants.expected: Viscera Seer's sacrifice has already been used. The Bombardment activation is not legal (can_play is false): A controls no other creature to sacrifice. B stays at 20.

variants.label: second_creature
variants.delta: A also controls Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: The Bombardment activation is legal, paid by sacrificing Grizzly Bears. When it resolves B takes 1 damage and is at 19; the Seer's scry also resolves.

scenarios.title: A cost whose action a replacement effect modified still counts as paid
decisions: A activates Goblin Bombardment, sacrificing Grizzly Bears, targeting player B.
Both players pass; the ability resolves.

variants.label: replaced_sacrifice
variants.expected: Rest in Peace replaces the graveyard move: Grizzly Bears is exiled instead of put into the graveyard. The cost still counts as paid, so Goblin Bombardment's ability resolves and B takes 1 damage, ending at 19.

variants.label: no_replacement
variants.delta: Rest in Peace is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is put into A's graveyard as the cost. The ability resolves and B is at 19.

variants.label: nothing_to_sacrifice
variants.delta: Grizzly Bears is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: A controls no creature, so the activation is not legal (can_play is false) and B stays at 20.

scenarios.title: An if-you-do clause after a resolution-time cost depends on being able to pay it
decisions: B casts Shock targeting player A, tapping Mountain. Standstill's trigger goes on the stack above Shock.
A makes no response.
Both players pass; the trigger resolves, then Shock resolves.

variants.label: sacrifice_paid
variants.expected: On resolution of the trigger Standstill is sacrificed (the cost is paid), so each opponent of B draws three cards: A draws three Islands. Shock then deals 2 to A, leaving A at 18.

variants.label: destroyed_in_response
variants.delta: Instead of making no response, A activates Seal of Cleansing in response to the trigger, sacrificing it, targeting Standstill.
variants.expected: Standstill is destroyed before the trigger resolves. When the trigger resolves, Standstill cannot be sacrificed, so nobody draws. Shock deals 2 to A, leaving A at 18; A's library still has four Islands.

scenarios.forge_notes: Seal of Cleansing's activation is not a spell, so it does not trigger Standstill.

scenarios.title: An unless clause applies its effect only when the player does not pay
decisions: A casts Shock targeting player B, tapping one Mountain.
B responds with Force Spike targeting Shock, tapping Island.
When Force Spike resolves, A declines to pay {1}; the second Mountain stays untapped.
Both players pass; the remaining stack resolves.

variants.label: declines_to_pay
variants.expected: Force Spike's effect happens: Shock is countered and goes to A's graveyard. B stays at 20.

variants.label: pays
variants.delta: A pays {1} by tapping the second Mountain instead of declining.
variants.expected: Force Spike does nothing: Shock is not countered and resolves, dealing 2 to B, who is at 18.

scenarios.title: An if-you-do clause after an optional search checks the choice to search, not the result

setup.notes: Library is listed top card first.

decisions: At the beginning of A's upkeep Elfhame Sanctuary triggers; A chooses to search and finds Forest.
The trigger resolves and play moves on to the draw step.

variants.label: search_finds_land
variants.expected: Forest is put into A's hand, the library is shuffled, and A skips the draw step. A's hand is Forest; Shock stays in the library.

variants.label: search_finds_nothing
variants.delta: A's library holds Lightning Bolt instead of Forest, so the search finds no basic land.
variants.expected: No card is found, the library is shuffled, and A still skips the draw step because A chose to search. A's hand is empty and Shock and Lightning Bolt stay in the library.

variants.label: declines_search
variants.delta: A chooses not to search.
variants.expected: The draw step is not skipped: A draws the top card, Shock. A's hand is Shock and Forest stays in the library.

scenarios.forge_notes: Depends on Forge running the SkipPhase subability when the optional search finds no card.

scenarios.title: Mana may be spent as though it were mana of any type when an effect allows it
decisions: A casts Raging Goblin ({R}), paying {R} with {W} from Plains.

variants.label: vizier
variants.expected: Vizier of the Menagerie lets A spend mana as though it were mana of any type on creature spells, so {W} pays {R}. The cast is legal (can_play is true) and Raging Goblin enters the battlefield.

variants.label: no_vizier
variants.delta: Vizier of the Menagerie is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: {W} cannot pay {R}, so Raging Goblin cannot be cast (can_play is false).

scenarios.forge_notes: A's library is empty and nothing is drawn; Vizier's look-at-top and cast-from-top statics have nothing to act on.
